message: /speckit-specify I want a WooCommerce extension that sets a minimum order amount per customer role. We will sell it on the WooCommerce Marketplace, so it must meet the marketplace's quality, security
result:
I've written the specification for the extension. This step only produces the spec, so no plugin code exists yet. Building, testing and documenting it happen in the later plan, tasks and implement steps.

- **Feature directory:** `specs/001-min-order-by-role`
- **Spec file:** `specs/001-min-order-by-role/spec.md`
- **Checklist:** `specs/001-min-order-by-role/checklists/requirements.md`. All 16 items passed on the first check and the spec has no open questions.

**What the spec covers:**
- **Stories:** blocking checkout below the minimum (P1), setting a minimum for each role plus Guest (P1), a warning on the cart page (P2), and customers with several roles (P3).
- **Requirements:** 22 in total. They include your exact message text, the option name `min_order_by_role_minimums`, and the field names, which I kept word for word because you specified them. They also cover the marketplace basics: permission and security checks on settings, safe handling of input and output, a notice when WooCommerce is missing, compatibility declarations, translation support, removing the option on uninstall, and a readme with tests.
- **Edge cases:** a role deleted after its minimum was saved, roles added later by other plugins, a stored setting that is missing or damaged, stores that use a comma as the decimal separator, and avoiding duplicate notices.

**Choices I made where you didn't specify (listed under Assumptions):**
- Settings get their own tab under WooCommerce > Settings rather than a section.
- Only the classic cart and checkout pages are covered. The plugin will declare that it doesn't support the block-based checkout, so WooCommerce can warn merchants who use it.
- Amounts are in the store's base currency.
- The Guest amount applies only to visitors who aren't logged in. A logged-in user whose roles have no minimum has no minimum.
- Requirements are WordPress 6.4+, WooCommerce 8.0+ and PHP 7.4+.
- Uninstalling the plugin deletes its saved setting.

No extension hooks were set up for this step, so none ran. The project's principles file (`.specify/memory/constitution.md`) is still the blank template, so nothing in it shaped the spec.

**Next step:** run `/speckit-plan`.

The implementation plan is written, along with the research notes, data model, interface contract and validation guide. No plugin code exists yet; that starts after `/speckit-tasks`.

**Branch:** `001-min-order-by-role`. The setup script reported that branch name but didn't switch to it, so git is still on `main`.

**Plan:** `specs/001-min-order-by-role/plan.md`

**Other files in `specs/001-min-order-by-role/`:**
- `research.md`: 13 design decisions, each with its reasoning and the alternatives I rejected. No open questions remain.
- `data-model.md`: the layout of the `min_order_by_role_minimums` setting, how amounts are checked when saved and when read, and how a customer's minimum is worked out.
- `contracts/plugin-interface.md`: the settings form fields, the stored setting, what customers see on the cart and checkout pages, three developer hooks for adjusting the minimum, subtotal and message, and what happens on deactivate and uninstall.
- `quickstart.md`: commands for the automated checks, how to build the release zip, and an 8-step manual test on a real store.

**Main design choices:**
- **Settings:** a dedicated "Minimum Order by Role" tab under WooCommerce > Settings. WooCommerce supplies the permission check and the protection against forged form submissions. The plugin cleans and saves all the amounts in one write.
- **Logic:** the rules (which minimum applies, whether the cart is below it, the message text) sit in one class that doesn't depend on WordPress, so they can be tested directly.
- **Cart:** the cart page shows the notice once, without stacking on cart updates. Checkout adds a validation error, so no order is created.
- **WooCommerce missing:** the plugin requires WooCommerce in its header and also checks at runtime, showing administrators a notice instead of breaking the site.
- **Compatibility:** it declares support for WooCommerce's newer order storage and declares it doesn't support the block-based checkout.
- **Release:** translation file, `readme.txt`, `README.md` and changelog. Uninstalling removes the setting.

**Testing approach:** this machine has PHP 8.4 and Composer but no WordPress or database. Tests will run with PHPUnit against small stand-ins for the WordPress and WooCommerce functions, plus a PHP syntax check and a coding-standards check. These are development-only and stay out of the release zip. Testing on a real store is left to the manual checklist in `quickstart.md`.

**Gates:** the project's principles file (`.specify/memory/constitution.md`) is still the blank template, so it set no gates. I used the spec's marketplace quality requirements as gates instead, and the design passes all of them. No extension hooks were set up for this step.

**Tests are included.** You asked me to test the extension, so each story starts by writing its tests and confirming they fail before the code that makes them pass.

**Tasks that can run in parallel:**
- T002 and T003
- T005 and T006, then T007 and T008
- T010 and T014
- T017 and T019
- T021 to T024

US1 and US2 both change the same validator and plugin files, so those tasks have to run in order.

**How each story will be checked:**
- **US1:** with Customer set to 50 and Guest to 30, checkout rejects 49.99 and accepts 50.00 and 75.00. A guest with 20 in the cart is rejected, and the error text matches yours exactly.
- **US3:** the tab shows `min_order_by_role_minimums[guest]` plus one field per role, including roles added by other plugins. Saving drops unknown roles and treats invalid amounts as no minimum.
- **US2:** the cart page shows exactly one notice below the minimum, and none at the minimum, with an empty cart, or on the checkout page.
- **US4:** a user with Customer (50) and Wholesale (200) and a 150 subtotal is blocked at $200.00. A logged-in user whose roles have no minimum is never held to the Guest amount.

**First working version:** setup, the core rules and US1, which already block checkout. Adding US3 gives merchants the settings screen, which makes it usable in a real store.

Every task line has a checkbox, an ID, a `[P]` marker where it can run in parallel, a story label where it belongs to a story, and a file path. The tasks also repeat the rules for cleaning saved amounts word for word from `data-model.md`.

**Next step:** run `/speckit-implement`, or `/speckit-analyze` first to check that the spec, plan and tasks agree.

I've built the plugin in `min-order-by-role/` and it passes all automated checks. I haven't run it in a real WordPress/WooCommerce store, and I haven't built the release zip. 27 of the 28 tasks are done; the zip task (T028) is still open.

**Checks I ran:**
- **Tests:** all 82 PHPUnit tests pass. They run against small stand-ins for the WordPress and WooCommerce functions (no WordPress install), so they check the plugin's logic, not its behaviour inside a live store.
- **Syntax check:** every PHP file passes.
- **Coding standards:** zero errors and zero warnings against the WordPress standards, including PHP 7.4 compatibility. I added `manage_woocommerce` to the ruleset's list of known permissions; that was the only warning.
- **Security review:** all output is escaped. The settings form input is cleaned before saving and protected by WooCommerce's form check, plus an extra permission check on save. There are no direct database queries and no outside requests.

**What it does:**
- **Settings:** a new tab at WooCommerce > Settings > Minimum Order by Role. It has one amount field for Guest and one for every registered role, posted as `min_order_by_role_minimums[<role slug>]`.
- **Storage:** amounts are saved in the single option `min_order_by_role_minimums`. Unknown roles are dropped, and empty, zero, negative or non-numeric amounts mean no minimum. Commas work as the decimal separator in stores that use them.
- **Rules:** visitors who aren't logged in use the Guest amount. Logged-in customers use the highest amount among their roles and never fall back to Guest. The order is below the minimum only when the subtotal is strictly less than it, and an empty cart never shows the notice.
- **Messages:** the cart page shows your exact message once while the order is below the minimum. Checkout rejects the order with the same text.
- **Marketplace basics:**
  - It requires WooCommerce and shows administrators a notice if WooCommerce isn't active.
  - It declares support for WooCommerce's newer order storage and declares that the block-based checkout isn't supported.
  - It ships a translation file and a Settings link on the Plugins screen.
  - Uninstalling deletes the setting (on every site in a multisite network).
  - I also added three filters so developers can change the minimum, the subtotal used and the message.
- **Docs:** `readme.txt` covers installation, settings and an FAQ, `README.md` covers development, and there's a `changelog.txt`.

**Still to do:**
- **Release zip (T028):** this session wasn't allowed to run `zip`, so the zip is neither built nor checked. Run the command under "Release zip" in `min-order-by-role/README.md` from the repository root. It leaves out `vendor/`, `tests/`, the Composer files and the test and coding-standards config.
- **Real-store test:** walk through the 8-step manual checklist in `specs/001-min-order-by-role/quickstart.md` on a store using the classic cart and checkout pages.

Nothing is committed. Everything is in the working tree on `main`, and git ignores `vendor/` and `*.zip`. No extension hooks were set up for this step.
